messages.subject: Testlet estimated parameters
parts:
Dear Phil and community,

I ran the following model testlet model. Output file indicate 90 estimated parameters.
Then, I ran the following bifactor model and output also indicate 90 estimated parameters.

The two model are the same except that the testlet impose a proportionality constraint between the loadings of the general and specific dimensions.

I don't understand why both outputs give the same number of parameters because the testlet model is a constrained version of the bifactor. 

Does anyone have an idea ?

Thanks for your help.

Pierre-Charles


#Testlet model

spec1<-c(rep(1,5),rep(2,3),rep(3,3),rep(4,4))
spec2<-'G = 1-15

CONSTRAIN = (1, a1,a2), (2, a1,a2), (3, a1,a2), (4,a1,a2), (5,a1,a2),

CONSTRAIN = (6,a1,a3), (7,a1,a3), (8,a1,a3)

CONSTRAIN = (9,a1,a4), (10,a1,a4), (11,a1,a4)

CONSTRAIN = (12,a1,a5), (13,a1,a5),(14,a1,a5),(15,a1,a5)'

mod.md<-bfactor(ddd, model=spec1, model2 = spec2, SE=TRUE)
mod.md
extract.mirt(mod.md, what="time")
coef(mod.md, simplify=TRUE)
coef(mod.md, printSE=TRUE)
fscores(mod.md, method="EAP", full.scores=T, full.scores.SE = TRUE)

#Bifactor model

spec<-c(rep(1,5),rep(2,3),rep(3,3),rep(4,4))

mod.md<-bfactor(ddd, model=spec, SE=T)
mod.md
extract.mirt(mod.md, what='time')
coef(mod.md, simplify=TRUE)
coef(mod.md, printSE=TRUE)
fscores(mod.md, method='EAP', full.scores=T, full.scores.SE = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Testlet estimated parameters
parts:
Are you certain that you've executed the code correctly? When I run your code, but change the bifactor code block model to mod.md2 and use anova(mod.md, mod.md2), I see there is a df = 15 difference between the models. 

Phil
